args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — COUNTERPARTY MARKUP RECONCILIATION

CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
Prepared for internal review purposes

================================================================
LEGEND
================================================================
[ADDED] = Text inserted into the counterparty draft to conform to firm-standard requirements.
[DELETED] = Text stricken from the counterparty draft.
[COMMENT] = Drafting note/instruction, not operative text.

================================================================
REDLINE — SECTION-BY-SECTION
================================================================

**Section 1 — Definitions**

*1.1 "Material Adverse Effect"*

[DELETE existing counterparty definition:]

"Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, circumstance, development or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has a material adverse effect on the business, condition (financial or otherwise), assets, liabilities or results of operations of the Company, **excluding any event, change, circumstance, development or effect arising from or relating to any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation or proceeding** [DELETED — counterparty-added carve-out for regulatory action].

[ADD firm-standard definition:]

"Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, circumstance, development or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, is or would reasonably be expected to be materially adverse to the business, condition (financial or otherwise), assets, liabilities, results of operations, or prospects of the Company or the counterparty, pursuant to the firm-standard definition at Section 1.01 of the internal playbook. No exceptions, carve-outs, or qualifiers shall be implied unless expressly set forth herein.

[COMMENT:] The counterparty's proposed deletion of regulatory action from the definition of MAE is rejected. The disclosure at Schedule 3.7 identifies two pending regulatory inquiries. Excluding regulatory action from MAE would deprive the client of a material adverse effect remedy precisely for the risks already identified. This carve-out is off-market and inconsistent with the executed credit agreement, which contains no such exclusion. MAE must capture all events including regulatory developments.

*1.2 "Indemnification Cap"*

[Current counterparty text — as revised:]
"Indemnification Cap" means an amount equal to **[X reduced amount — see below]** of the aggregate consideration payable.

[INSERT firm-standard:] The Indemnification Cap shall be equal to ten percent (10%) of the aggregate consideration, or such higher amount as set forth in the executed credit agreement, and shall not be reduced other than by express written agreement of the parties. [COMMENT: The counterparty's silent reduction of the cap is rejected.]

*1.3 "Basket" (Deductible vs. Tipping)*

[CURRENT — counterparty markup converts to a tipping basket:]
"Basket" means the amount of losses that must be exceeded in the aggregate before the indemnifying party shall be liable for all losses, including those below the threshold.

[COMMENT — CLIENT CONCESSION:] Consistent with the controlling partner instruction in the deal correspondence, the client will accept the counterparty's conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. This is a negotiated concession and the redline reflects this as accepted by the client.

*1.4 "Survival Period"*

[CURRENT — counterparty markup shortens survival:]
"Survival Period" means, [with respect to the core representations, a period of [X] months from the Closing Date] [DELETED — walk-away issue].

[INSERT firm-standard:] "Survival Period" means, with respect to the Core Representations (including, without limitation, representations relating to regulatory compliance, financial statements, and title to assets), the period ending on the date that is the later of (i) the applicable statute of limitations plus sixty (60) days, and (ii) twenty-four (24) months from the Closing Date, in each case consistent with Exhibit B (Survival Matrix) to the executed credit agreement and the internal playbook.

[COMMENT — WALK-AWAY ISSUE:] The counterparty's reduction of the survival period for core representations is a walk-away issue under the controlling partner instruction. The survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B to the executed credit agreement and the internal playbook establishes the firmer-survival standard. Any reduction of the survival period for the core representations is unacceptable and must be restored to the Exhibit B standard.

================================================================
SCHEDULE RECONCILIATION
================================================================

**Schedule 3.7 — Pending Regulatory Inquiries**

The counterparty's markup modifies the MAE definition to add carve-outs for regulatory action. Schedule 3.7 discloses two (2) pending regulatory inquiries affecting the Company. These pending inquiries intersect directly with the MAE carve-out proposed by the counterparty.

[ADD:] The disclosures in Schedule 3.7 shall be deemed incorporated into the definition of Material Adverse Effect for all purposes under this Agreement. To the extent of any conflict between this Agreement and Schedule 3.7, the disclosures in Schedule 3.7 shall control.

[COMMENT:] Because Schedule 3.7 specifically discloses pending regulatory inquiries, and because the counterparty simultaneously seeks to exempt regulatory action from the MAE definition, the net effect would be to strip the client of any MAE-based remedy for the very regulatory exposure identified in the disclosure schedule. The scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials—this is not a matter of mere drafting preference. The MAE carve-out must be rejected and the Schedule 3.7 disclosures recognized.

**Schedule 5.2 — Retained Liabilities**

Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the counterparty's indemnification changes would silently shift to the client.

[ADD:] The retained liabilities identified in Schedule 5.2 shall remain the sole responsibility of the counterparty, and shall not be treated as losses subject to the indemnification provisions of this Agreement to the extent the reduction of the indemnification cap or the basket modifications would otherwise shift such liabilities to the client.

[COMMENT:] The concurrent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket, when read together with the retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2, would result in a silent transfer of economic exposure. The retained liabilities must be excluded from any indemnification limitations.

**Exhibit B — Survival Matrix**

Exhibit B sets forth the survival matrix for representations and warranties. The counterparty's markup introduces a new limitation period that contradicts Exhibit B.

[ADD:] Exhibit B (Survival Matrix) is incorporated by reference and shall control over any conflicting provision in the body of this Agreement, including any purported shortening of the survival period for core representations.

[COMMENT:] The survival matrix in Exhibit B establishes the term of survival for each representation category. The counterparty's "new limitation period" that "shortens survival for the core representations" directly contradicts Exhibit B. Per the controlling instruction, this is a walk-away issue.

================================================================
ADDITIONAL REQUIRED MODIFICATIONS
================================================================

**A. Indemnification Cap Restoration**

The counterparty's markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. Restore the cap to the full firm-standard amount. The silent reduction is particularly problematic when combined with:
- the basket conversion (partial concession accepted by client per controlling instruction);
- Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities (which the cap reduction would shift to the client).

**B. Indemnification Basket — Client Concession Reflected**

Consistent with the controlling partner instruction, the client concedes the basket conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket. The redline reflects this accepted change. The client should not expend negotiation capital on this point.

**C. Survival Period — Walk-Away Issue, No Acceptance**

The counterparty's limitation-period change shortens survival for the core representations. Per the controlling instruction, ANY survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. The redline restores the survival period for core representations to the Exhibit B matrix standard. If the counterparty persists, the client's fallback position is:
1. First position: Full restoration per Exhibit B.
2. No compromise below Exhibit B standard.

**D. MAE Definition — No Carve-Out for Regulatory Action**

Reject the MAE carve-out for regulatory action in its entirety. Schedule 3.7's disclosures of pending regulatory inquiries make this carve-out particularly pernicious. The definition must be restored to the firm-standard language from the internal playbook and the executed credit agreement.

**E. Schedule 3.7, 5.2, and Exhibit B Integration**

Each of the schedules and exhibits must be fully integrated into the operative provisions of the agreement, with express statement in the body that such schedules control over conflicting provisions in the body.

================================================================
END OF REDLINE
================================================================

MEMORANDUM

TO: Engagement Partner
FROM: Deal Team
DATE: [Current Date]
RE: Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review: Issues/Risk Memorandum

CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT / ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

We have reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement against the (i) internal playbook, (ii) executed credit agreement, (iii) depository bank's standard form, (iv) account details, and (v) related correspondence and checklists. The counterparty's markup introduces three (3) material deviations from the firm-standard baseline:

1. **Indemnification Cap Reduction & Basket Conversion** — the cap is silently reduced and the basket is converted from a deductible to a tipping basket;
2. **Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Carve-Outs** — adding carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter; and
3. **Survival Period Reduction** — a new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

Consistent with the controlling partner instruction in the deal correspondence (latest email controls), the **basket conversion is conceded**, but **any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue**. The MAE carve-out, the indemnification cap reduction, and all associated schedule interactions are also addressed below.

A summary deviation matrix is provided at Section VII.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
II. DEVIATION 1: INDemnIFICATION CAP REDUCTION & BASKET CONVERSION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Section References:** Indemnification section; Definitions of "Indemnification Cap" and "Basket"; Schedule 5.2.

**Playbook Requirement:** The internal playbook requires an indemnification cap equal to ten percent (10%) of aggregate consideration (or the higher amount specified in the executed credit agreement), and a deductible-type basket structure with losses below the threshold borne by the indemnified party.

**Counterparty Deviation:**
(a) The indemnification cap is **silently reduced** — no companion markup or disclosure accompanies the reduction.
(b) The basket is **converted from a deductible to a tipping basket** — under a tipping basket, once losses exceed the threshold, the indemnifying party becomes liable for losses from the first dollar (and below the threshold).

**Risk Rating:** HIGH (for the cap reduction); MODERATE (for the basket conversion).

**Exposure Analysis:**
- The reduction of the indemnification cap, when combined with the retained liabilities identified in Schedule 5.2, would **silently shift economic exposure** from the counterparty to the client. The retained liabilities listed in Schedule 5.2 that the markup's indemnification changes would shift include items that should remain the counterparty's sole responsibility.
- The basket conversion changes the loss-allocation structure. Under a deductible, the client would bear losses up to the threshold. Under a tipping basket, the client would bear losses up to the threshold but the counterparty would then become liable for all losses from the first dollar. The practical impact depends on the quantum of losses relative to the threshold.
- The interaction of the cap reduction and the basket conversion creates a compounding adverse effect: the client is both exposed to a lower aggregate cap (less protection) and a different loss-allocation structure.

**Client Concession:** Per the controlling partner instruction, the client will **concede the basket conversion**. No further negotiation capital should be spent on this point.

**Recommended Position on Cap Reduction:** **REJECT and restore** the cap to the firm-standard amount. If the counterparty persists, propose as a fallback that the cap reduction apply only to non-core breaches and that no cap reduction apply to fraud, willful misconduct, or breaches of the core representations.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION 2: MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Section References:** Definition of "Material Adverse Effect"; Schedule 3.7.

**Playbook Requirement:** The internal playbook and the executed credit agreement define "Material Adverse Effect" without carve-outs based on the source of the adverse effect. The firm-standard definition covers any material adverse effect on the business, including those arising from regulatory action, investigation, or proceeding.

**Counterparty Deviation:** The counterparty adds carve-outs to the MAE definition excluding "any event, change, circumstance, development or effect arising from or relating to any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation or proceeding" from the MAE determination.

**Risk Rating:** CRITICAL / HIGH.

**Exposure Analysis:**
- **Direct conflict with Schedule 3.7:** Schedule 3.7 discloses **two (2) pending regulatory inquiries** affecting the Company. The counterparty's MAE carve-out would exclude the very regulatory actions already disclosed and pending. The net effect is that the client would have **no MAE-based remedy** if these regulatory inquiries were to result in a material adverse effect.
- **Market practice:** It is not market-standard to exclude regulatory action of the kind at issue from the MAE definition, particularly where those inquiries have been affirmatively disclosed. The carved-out category tracks the exact risk disclosed, indicating that the carve-out is designed to neutralize the client's MAE protection.
- **Regulatory framework:** The disclosure at Schedule 3.7 is a baseline fact. The client's diligence identified these inquiries; the counterparty now seeks to eliminate the client's contractual protection against the consequences of those same inquiries.
- **Precedent:** The executed credit agreement contains no such carve-out. The depository bank's standard form likewise contains no regulatory-action exclusion from MAE.

**Recommended Position:** **REJECT** the MAE carve-out in its entirety. This deviation must be removed. If the counterparty insists on some variant, the maximum acceptable concession would be to (i) confirm the carve-out does not apply to the specific regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and (ii) exclude any clause that would exclude regulatory action that predates the execution of this Agreement. However, given the intersection with Schedule 3.7 disclosures, the recommended position is a **hard reject** with no negotiation.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. DEVIATION 3: SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION (WALK-AWAY ISSUE)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Section References:** Survival/limitation provisions; Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).

**Playbook Requirement:** Exhibit B to the executed credit agreement sets forth the survival matrix, which establishes the survival period for each category of representations and warranties, including the core representations. The internal playbook requires survival for core representations through the applicable statute of limitations plus sixty (60) days, subject to a minimum of twenty-four (24) months.

**Counterparty Deviation:** The counterparty introduces a "new limitation period" that **shortens survival for the core representations**.

**Risk Rating:** CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY.

**Exposure Analysis:**
- **Direct contradiction of Exhibit B:** The survival matrix in Exhibit B is a defined and controlling exhibit. The counterparty's new limitation period directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival terms.
- **Core representations:** Shortening the survival period for core representations fundamentally undermines the client's remedial rights. Core representations typically include representations about the Company's financial condition, title to assets, regulatory compliance (of direct relevance given the Schedule 3.7 inquiries), and authority.
- **Controlling instruction:** The partner email thread explicitly identifies **ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue**. This is the controlling instruction; earlier messages stating a different priority ordering are superseded.
- **Risk symmetry:** A reduced survival period benefits the counterparty (shortening its exposure window) and harms the client (shortening the client's time to discover and assert a misrepresentation claim). Given the pending regulatory inquiries identified in Schedule 3.7, regulatory-related misrepresentations could surface well after a shortened survival window.

**Recommended Position:** **WALK-AWAY** — No acceptance of any survival-period reduction for the core representations. Exhibit B's survival matrix must be restored in full. This is non-negotiable. If the counterparty does not withdraw the new limitation period, the deal should not close. The client should be prepared to walk away from the transaction if this issue is not resolved.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
V. CROSS-CUTTING ISSUES AND INTERACTIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**A. Schedule 3.7 / MAE Carve-Out Interaction**

The counterparty's MAE carve-out excludes regulatory action; Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. The schedule is made part of the base materials. The "scheduled exceptions control over general statements." Therefore, even if the counterparty argues that the carve-out is a general statement, the specific disclosures in Schedule 3.7 should override it. The deal team should ensure that the agreement expressly states that Schedule 3.7 disclosures control.

**B. Schedule 5.2 / Indemnification Interaction**

Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The indemnification cap reduction and basket conversion, read together, would shift portions of these retained liabilities to the client. The redline must ensure that Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities are excluded from the indemnification framework altogether or ring-fenced against any cap or basket limitations.

**C. Exhibit B / Survival Interaction**

Exhibit B's survival matrix is a controlling baseline. Any competing survival-period language in the body of the draft (whether from the counterparty or otherwise) must conform to Exhibit B. The redline must include an express integration clause stating that Exhibit B controls.

**D. Cumulative Effect Assessment**

The three deviations, taken together, create a materially worse risk profile for the client than the firm-standard baseline:
| Combination | Effect |
|---|---|
| Cap reduction + Basket conversion | Lower aggregate recovery; different loss allocation structure |
| MAE carve-out + Schedule 3.7 | No MAE remedy for disclosed regulatory exposure |
| Survival reduction + Exhibit B | Shorter remedy window for core representations |
| All three combined | Multidimensional erosion of client's risk protections |

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
VI. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATING STRATEGY AND PRIORITIES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

1. **Hard red line / walk-away:** Survival period reduction (Deviations 3). Any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue per controlling instruction. Do not compromise.
2. **Hard reject:** MAE carve-out (Deviations 2) given the direct intersection with Schedule 3.7 disclosures.
3. **Reject and restore:** Indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 1a). Restore full cap.
4. **Concede:** Basket conversion (Deviation 1b) per controlling instruction. Do not expend negotiation capital.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------
